summary: Sidebar — the primary navigation rail, and the first consumer of the --ui-nav-* role family, which had sat in the contract since Phase 1 without ever being rendered. Built as a plain <nav> rather than a behaviour-layer component: navigation is links, and Tab order, Enter activation, middle-click and open-in-new-tab are worth more than the arrow keys a roving-tabindex menu would buy at their expense (ARIA APG — a nav is not a menu). Composed as SLOTS, not links: the design's own layer names (Nav Group, Primary Level Item, Second Level Item, Spacer) describe rows, and one of those rows holds a search field while another holds a whole Progress bar — so Sidebar.Item takes an OPTIONAL href and renders an <a> only when given one. An anchor wrapping a form control is invalid, and a row that cannot hold one cannot draw the sheet. Sidebar.Section carries the second level with isCollapsible OFF by default, because the sheet draws a chevron on 'Brand' and none on 'Most recent'; a header that cannot collapse renders as a span rather than a button that does nothing. Rows inside a Section are <li>, rows outside one are not, since announcing a search field as a list item misdescribes the page. Both levels sit at the same 24px inset (8 on the body plus 16 on the row) and are told apart by weight and ink — an indent would be a redundant second signal costing room on a narrow rail. The current page is ANNOUNCED via aria-current and changes weight too, because the active fill measures barely over 1:1 against the rail. Four tooling and token defects the component exposed, all first-of-its-kind: --ui-nav-width and --ui-nav-rail-width had NO Tailwind utility at all, the same gap --ui-scrim had before Modal, and now emit into the spacing namespace as w-nav / w-nav-rail; the nav colour family was the only one the emitter never remapped, so it minted the stuttering bg-nav-bg and text-nav-ink, now bg-nav, text-ink-nav, bg-nav-active, text-ink-nav-active and border-edge-nav; --ui-nav-ink-muted on --ui-nav-bg was rendered by every second-level item while absent from CONTRAST_PAIRS, caught by the contrast gate added hours earlier; and the rail's 16px type was first written as text-title-sm, which is a FLUID role — it computed to 12.17px in Chromium and would be smallest on a phone, the one viewport where the sheet actually draws this rail. A fixed-width surface takes fixed type roles, so both levels are text-body-lg. axe also caught the BrandThemed story rendering two <nav> landmarks with the same name — a landmark-unique violation, and exactly what the required `label` prop exists to prevent. Design defects corrected: a raw 16px rail radius and a run of raw 4/8/16px paddings became scale tokens, and the active item used --ui-bg-elevated rather than --ui-nav-active-bg, which is the whole reason the nav family exists.

migration.manual: The nav utilities are RENAMED: bg-nav-bg becomes bg-nav, text-nav-ink becomes text-ink-nav, bg-nav-active-bg becomes bg-nav-active, text-nav-active-ink becomes text-ink-nav-active, and border-nav-border becomes border-edge-nav. Nothing consumed them before Sidebar, so no shipped component changes.
